{{Short description|Scottish mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2022}}
'''Penelope Jane Davies''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|OBE}} is a Scottish [[mathematician]] who in 2009 became the second female president of the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]], after [[Elizabeth McHarg]].{{r|emspres|3pres}} Her research involves numerical simulation of the [[partial differential equation]]s describing [[Scattering theory|wave scattering]] and elastic stability and biomechanical modelling. She is a senior lecturer in mathematics and statistics at the [[University of Strathclyde]].{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Davies earned her Ph.D. in 1987 from [[Heriot-Watt University]] under the supervision of [[John M. Ball|John MacLeod Ball]];{{r|mg}} her dissertation was ''Stability problems in nonlinear elasticity''.{{r|diss}} She was on the staff of the [[University of Dundee]] before moving to the University of Strathclyde.{{r|dundee}}

She was the President of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society from 2009 to 2011.{{r|emspres|3pres}}

==Recognition==
Davies was made an Officer of the Order of the British Empire "for services to mathematics" in the [[2014 Birthday Honours]].{{r|bh}}
